clue.text: Pop Scotsman composed entertains One Direction

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside your home, so one piece goes within the other
composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Scottish pop composer writes a tune for the boy band One Direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One Direction' reads as the boy band's name, but One is the inserted I and Direction alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: North, south-east and the like are bearings marked on a compass, each one a direction.

clue.text: 1960s rock band's stuff filled with energy

indicators.note: something filled with another thing holds it inside

parts.note: to stuff is to cram
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: The possessions of a sixties band packed with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: Cream was the British rock trio of Eric Clapton, Jack Bruce and Ginger Baker.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream were a celebrated British rock group formed in 1966.

clue.text: Chap I healed with beautiful hands?

parts.note: a chap is a man
to be healed is to be cured

explanation.surface: A man says he was cured by the touch of lovely hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'beautiful hands' means hands with groomed nails.
explanation.definitionFit: Manicured hands have had their nails trimmed and polished, so look well kept.

clue.text: Place to put picture frame for exhibition — it's white

parts.note: a photo album is where pictures are kept

indicators.note: a frame is the edge around a picture, so the outside letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Choosing a spot and a frame for a picture going on show; it's white.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is the white of an egg, a clear substance that turns white when cooked.

clue.text: Maybe top criminal seizing power

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the criminal holds power inside

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Perhaps a leading crook is seizing control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like boss; it is the spinning toy, an example of something that spins.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning top is one kind of spinner, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Old hands grasping answer in language exam?

indicators.note: hands grasp things, holding them inside

parts.note: R and L, right and left hands

explanation.surface: Aged hands holding an answer paper in a foreign language test.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a regular part of foreign language tests.

clue.text: Wind Harry Potter's friend up before festival

indicators.note: the friend's name comes before the festival in the answer
in a down answer up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Ron Weasley is Harry Potter's best friend
Easter is a Christian festival

explanation.surface: A young wizard's friend is up early for the Easter holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A nor'easter is a strong wind or storm blowing from the north-east.

clue.text: Joke suitable for all by a Biblical character

parts.note: to josh is to joke or tease
U is the British film certificate meaning universal, suitable for all ages

explanation.surface: A family-friendly joke told by a Bible figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshua led the Israelites after Moses and has an Old Testament book named after him.

clue.text: Second husband boarding air-conditioned train

indicators.note: boarding a train means getting in it, so the husband goes inside

parts.note: air-conditioned means kept cool
H is the genealogy abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A second husband climbs onto a cool, air-conditioned train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway train; it is the verb meaning to educate.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or drill them in a skill.

clue.text: Starters of organic cod eaten — and now the main

indicators.note: starters are the first courses, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A menu note: an organic cod starter is eaten, and now the main course arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' looks like the main course of the meal; it is an old poetic name for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main, as in the Spanish Main, is a literary term for the open sea, of which a vast body is an ocean.

clue.text: Setter caught wearing two lingerie items and 100 trinkets

indicators.note: the setter and the catch are dressed in the bras, so they go inside those letters

parts.note: a pair of bras
the setter refers to himself as I
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A setter is caught wearing two bras, along with a hundred cheap ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: IC goes after the first BR, giving BR-IC-ABRA, and the Roman C ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bric-a-brac is a jumble of small ornaments and curios of little value, much like trinkets.

clue.text: Return from foolish mooching around capitals in Middle East

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the capitals, which sit inside them
a foolish arrangement is a silly, muddled one, so the letters of mooching are reshuffled
capitals are capital letters, so the first letter of each of the next two words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone back from loafing aimlessly about the capital cities of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' is a noun here, an arrival back home, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A homecoming is an arrival back at home, a return after time away.

clue.text: Dressing always kept by doctor

indicators.note: held or kept by something means sitting inside it

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
ay (or aye) is an old word meaning always or ever

explanation.surface: A doctor who keeps a constant supply of salad dressing on hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is the casual short form of mayonnaise, a creamy sauce used on salads.

clue.text: Aiming to get slightly reduced number

indicators.note: slightly reduced means cut back by a little, here a single letter off the end

parts.note: aiming for something is aspiring to it

explanation.surface: Someone setting out to cut back a figure by a small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a figure; read it as something that numbs, a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: A number here is a thing that numbs pain, and this common tablet is a painkiller.

clue.text: Mix of dried flowers and grass — chuck it down drain, periodically

parts.note: grass and pot are both slang for cannabis
chuck it down is British slang for rain heavily, to pour

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Dried flowers and cannabis are tipped down the drain in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a scented blend of dried petals and spices kept in a bowl.

clue.text: Reading City mostly overwhelmed by Spanish team

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed by something is to be engulfed by it, so this goes inside the team

parts.note: Real Madrid, known as Real

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, the football club name

explanation.surface: A football report: Reading and Manchester City both beaten by Real Madrid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' reads as the English football club; it is the definition, a performance or recitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a public reading or performance of poems, music or prose.

clue.text: Doctor scowled at sign of fear

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor frowns at a patient showing signs of fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking into a cold sweat is a physical reaction to anxiety or terror.

clue.text: Fight participant in pugilism, a tad orthodox

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A boxer in a bout who fights in a slightly conventional style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fight' suggests boxing, but the fight is with a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull, so takes part in a bullfight.

clue.text: Complaint from old Tory PM clinging on to youth

indicators.note: clinging on to something means holding it tight, so the youth goes inside

parts.note: Theresa May, a former Conservative prime minister
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A grumble about a former Conservative leader hanging on to a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grievance; here it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment, and a malady is a disease.

clue.text: Asylum seeker good to enter EU, free to travel

indicators.note: the good goes in, entering the other letters
travel suggests moving around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A refugee wishes to enter the EU, free to move about.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is someone fleeing persecution who seeks safety and protection in another country.

clue.text: More intoxicated after friend gets Italian port

indicators.note: the shuffled word comes after the friend in the answer

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: intoxicated means drunk and reeling, so the letters of more are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gets drunker after a mate arrives in an Italian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Palermo is the capital of Sicily and a major seaport on its north coast.

clue.text: Playing poker outside empty casino in heat earlier

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit outside, around the other piece
playing with the letters means rearranging them
empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving the outer two

explanation.surface: Playing poker in a deserted casino earlier in the warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heat' is a verb here, and 'earlier' turns it into cooking in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To precook food is to cook it ahead of time before final heating.

clue.text: Batter in upturned polystyrene pots

indicators.note: upturned says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the following words, running across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook beating batter in overturned plastic pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' suggests pancake mix; it is a cricketer, and 'in' signals the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an opener is a batsman who starts the innings.

clue.text: Glance from king on throne

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: throne is a jokey word for the toilet, a loo in British slang
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch on his throne casts a quick glance.
explanation.walkthrough: The throne is not royal: it is slang for the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A look is a quick glance, as in 'take a look'.

clue.text: Eat dessert to start with? This has a nice smell

indicators.note: says the dessert word goes first, before the eating word

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding or dessert
to have something is to eat it, as in having lunch

explanation.surface: Should one eat pudding first? This tempting thing smells lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a scented lotion men put on the face after shaving, so it smells pleasant.

clue.text: Bad temper shown by fisherman dropping line

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so this letter is removed

parts.note: an angler is a fisherman

explanation.surface: A fisherman loses his line and loses his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is a strong feeling of annoyance or rage, a bad temper.

clue.text: Student that is getting university place

parts.note: L is for learner, a student driver's plate
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A student, that is, getting a university place.
explanation.definitionFit: In lieu of means in place of; lieu is an old word for place.

clue.text: Revolutionary Communist Party welcoming call for boldness

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so the call goes inside
revolutionary suggests a full turn, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist
a do is a party
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A radical communist party invites a call for daring action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a description of the party, but it only turns the Communist word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic courage and daring, a bold or reckless spirit.

clue.text: Sub-par performance from hunting dog with no lead

indicators.note: a dog with no lead is unleashed; here the leading letter is dropped

parts.note: a beagle is a small hound bred for hunting hares

explanation.surface: A hunting dog off its lead puts in a below-standard performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub-par' sounds like poor; in golf it means under par, which is good.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an eagle is a hole completed in two strokes under par, a score below par.

clue.text: Suppose river contains fish one's seen sliding on ice

indicators.note: contains means holds within, so the fish goes inside the other letters

parts.note: to figure is to suppose or reckon
a skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone supposes a river holds fish one can see slipping about on the frozen surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' places the fish between the supposing word and the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure skater performs jumps and spins while gliding over a rink.
